children: Orica bull Macquarie is pleased the explosives and chemicals company isn't planning for significant items or below-the-line restructuring costs next year. That "could improve profit quality," says the bank. Orica's FY 2026 net profit was weighed down by 325.5 million Australian dollars of significant items. The year prior, significant items totaled A$378.8 million. The company's balance sheet is strong, with leverage at the lower end of its target range, says Macquarie. That gives it capacity for potential bolt-on acquisitions, the bank says. Macquarie reiterates an outperform rating and raises its share-price target to A$26.60 from A$26.10. The stock is down 0.7% at A$23.655, after gaining 4.5% Thursday. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
